Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Functions - Generators


•  A generator is a function that returns an iterator that produces a sequence of values
  when iterated over.

•  Iterator - an object that can be iterated upon, i.e. we can traverse through all the values.

•  Generators in Python provides a way to create a function that behaves like an iterator.

•  Does not return a single value; instead, it returns an iterator object with a sequence of
   values.

• A yield statement is used instead of the return statement.

•   If the body of a def contains yield, the function automatically becomes a Python
   generator function.

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Generators

•  Syntax

def generator_function_name(arg):
      ………………………
       ………………………
       ………………………
             yield statement


• When the generator function  is called,  it does not execute the function body
   immediately. Instead,  it returns a generator object that can be iterated over to
  produce the values.

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Generators


Generator Object


•  Python Generator functions return a generator object that is iterable (used as
  an iterator).


•  Generator objects are accessed
    •  by calling the next method of the generator object (Refer Example 2)
       or
    •  using the generator object in a “for” loop (Refer Example 1)

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Generators


Example 1: Simple generator function that will yield three integers
(using for loop)

# Generator function
def generator_func():                                 Output:
    yieldyield 11                                        11
    yield 2                                        2
    yield 3                                                  3
# Code to check above generator function
for value in generator_func():
    print(value)

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):

Example 2: Simple generator function that will yield three integers
(using next() function)

# Generator function
def generator_func():
                                                      Output:    yield 10
    yield 20                                       1010
    yield 30                                       20
                                                  30
#obj is a generator object
obj=generator_func()

# Iterating over the generator object using next
print(next(obj))
print(next(obj))
print(next(obj))

Source slide page 9 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Generators

Pipelining Generators
Multiple generators can be used to pipeline a series of operations

Example: Compute the sum of squares of numbers in the Fibonacci
series
## GeneratorGenerator functionfunction - fibonaccifibonacci_numbersnumbers
def fibonacci_numbers(nums):
    x,y=0,1
    for i in range(nums):
        x,y=y,x+y                                   Output:
        yield x                                  6
# Generator function - square
def square(nums):
    for num in nums:
        yield num**2
print(sum(square(fibonacci_numbers(3))))

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Generators

Function Generators: yield vs. return

                      yield                         return
          Returns a value and pauses the execution  Returns a value and terminates the
           while maintaining the internal states       execution of the function
         UsedUsed toto convertconvert aa regularregular PythonPython        UsedUsed toto returnreturn thethe resultresult toto thethe callercaller
           function into a generator                 statement
         Used when the generator returns an      Used when a function is ready to send a
           intermediate result to the caller           value
         Code written after yield statement       Code written after return statement
          execute in next function call              won’t execute
                It can run multiple times                           It only runs a single time

 Note: We can’t include return inside a generator function. If we do, it will terminate the
 function.

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Functions - Generators

Function Generators: Summary

•  Python generator functions allows for the declaration of a function that behaves like an
   iterator, making it a faster, cleaner and easier way to create an iterator.


•  Generators are useful when we want to produce a large sequence of values, but we
   don't want to store all of them in memory at once.


•  The simplification of code is a result of generator function and generator expression
   support provided by Python.
